He played [[college basketball]] for [[American Eagles men's basketball|American University]], where he finished his four-year career as the school's fifth all-time leading scorer with 1,655 points. He made his NBA debut with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2018. Ingram is the [[NBA G League]]'s career leader in three-point field goals and games played. He has also scored the third-most points in league history and won the D-League 3-Point Contest in 2010 and 2016.{{cite web|last=Ramirez|first=Joey|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/180409-latest-laker-andre-ingram|title=Latest Laker: Andre Ingram|work=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2018|access-date=April 10, 2018}} As a pro, Ingram spent four seasons with the [[Utah Flash]] between 2007 and 2011, and four seasons with the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] between 2012 and 2016. After a short stint in Australia with the [[Perth Wildcats]], Ingram returned to the D-Fenders in March 2017. He continued on with the renamed South Bay Lakers for the 2017–18 season, before joining the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in April 2018, and finally making his [[NBA]] debut.{{Cite web |title=Lakers' Andre Ingram shines in hard-won NBA debut after 10 years in minors {{!}} Los Angeles Lakers {{!}} The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/apr/11/lakers-andre-ingram-nba-debut-rookie-persistence |access-date=2023-01-23 |website=amp.theguardian.com}} ==Early life== Ingram was born and raised in [[Richmond, Virginia]], and grew up in a tight-knit family of four. He loved basketball from an early age, and by the time he turned 12, he was beating his older brother by seven years, Lucius, in one-on-one.{{cite web|last=Faigen|first=Harrison|url=http://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2016/3/14/11208282/la-lakers-la-d-fenders-andre-ingram|title=Andre Ingram is the greatest three-point shooter you've never heard of|work=silverscreenandroll.com|date=March 14, 2016|access-date=October 18, 2016}} Ingram attended [[Highland Springs High School]] in [[Highland Springs, Virginia]], where he led the basketball team to the Group AAA championship as a senior in 2002–03, the first title in school history. That year, he averaged 22.8 points and 9.5 rebounds per game, while shooting 49 percent from three-point range. He was subsequently named the Associated Press Group AAA Player of the Year for his division. He left Highland Springs as a two-time Capital District Player of the Year and First-Team All-Metro, and as a senior was a First-Team All-State and First-Team All-Central Region pick.{{cite web|url=http://aueagles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ingram_andre00.html?view=bio|title=20 – Andre Ingram|work=AUEagles.com|access-date=October 18, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150124174912/http://aueagles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/ingram_andre00.html?view=bio|archive-date=January 24, 2015}} ==College career== ===Freshman year=== As a freshman at [[American Eagles men's basketball|American University]] in 2003–04, Ingram started in all 31 games and led the team with 13.6 points per game, which ranked fifth best in the league. He was subsequently named [[Patriot League]] Freshman of the Year, becoming the first American player to win the award. He had 16 points, five rebounds, two assists and two steals against Maryland on November 22, 2003, in his first collegiate game. On January 14, 2004, he made eight shots from behind the arc in a 27-point effort against Navy, which ties the second best single-game three-point total in AU history. In addition, his 15 three-point attempts against Navy is tied for the highest single-game attempt total for an Eagle. He went on to score a career-high 30 points on 10-of-19 shooting against Lafayette on February 28. ===Sophomore year=== As a sophomore in 2004–05, Ingram played in 28 games with 27 starts and was named first-team All-Patriot League. He finished the season as the PL's second-leading scoring, just half a point out of the lead, with 15.3 points per game. After being named the PL Preseason Player of the Year, Ingram opened the season with 38 points against VCU. He registered six 20+ point performances in 28 games, including two 30+ point performances. He was named Patriot League Player of the Week twice during February 2005, and at the season's end, he was named National Association of Basketball Coaches All-District 4 Second Team. ===Junior year=== As a junior in 2005–06, Ingram played and started in all 29 games. He led team in scoring for the third consecutive season, averaging 12.0 points per game. He scored in double digits in 19 of 29 games, starting the season with a 24-point effort against Washington on November 19. He notched his 1,000th career point, while amassing a season-high 10 rebounds, against the [[Saint Francis Red Flash men's basketball|Saint Francis Red Flash]] on January 2. At the season's end, he earned second-team All-Patriot League honors. ===Senior year=== As a senior in 2006–07, Ingram ranked fifth in the Patriot League in scoring (15.2 ppg), second in three-point field goal percentage (.424) and second in three-point field goals made per game (2.6). He scored 20 or more points eight times, including a season-high 25 points against Lafayette. He subsequently earned first-team All-Patriot League honors for the second time in three years.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/media/dleague/andre_ingram.pdf|title=Andre Ingram|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221214454/http://www.nba.com/media/dleague/andre_ingram.pdf|archive-date=December 21, 2016|url-status=dead}} Ingram finished his collegiate career as American's fifth all-time leading scorer with 1,655 points, as he led the team in scoring all four years. He graduated from American University with a bachelor’s degree in physics. ==Professional career== ===Utah Flash (2007–2011)=== On November 1, 2007, Ingram was selected by the [[Utah Flash]] in the seventh round of the [[2007 NBA Development League Draft]]. He spent four years with the Flash, and in that time, became the franchise's all-time leading scorer with 2,098 points. He also ranks second in rebounds (608), fourth in assists (336), and third in steals (184).{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Utah_Flash/16/Stats/Historical/Totals/All/points/All/desc/1/Regular_Season|title=Historical Utah Flash Stats|work=RealGM.com|access-date=October 18, 2016}} Ingram had a career-best year in 2009–10, as he won the [[Jason Collier Sportsmanship Award]] and participated in 2010 NBA D-League All-Star festivities in Dallas, where he took home the Three-Point Shooting Competition Championship. Ingram made noteworthy contributions in game as well, starting 49 of the team's 50 games, and averaging 12.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.5 steals in 34.0 minutes. He scored in double figures 36 times, including a season-high 24 points in a 104–99 road victory over the [[Bakersfield Jam]] on December 5, 2009.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/sportsmanship_100415.html |title=Utah's Andre Ingram Wins Jason Collier Sportsmanship Award |work=NBA.com |date=April 15, 2010 |access-date=October 18, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100418043253/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/sportsmanship_100415.html |archive-date=April 18, 2010 }} Following the 2010–11 season, the Flash suspended operations and left Ingram without a team for the 2011–12 season. ===Los Angeles D-Fenders (2012–2016)=== On March 22, 2012, Ingram was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/transactions_201112.html |title=2011-12 Transactions |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131031004037/http://www.nba.com/dleague/transactions_201112.html |archive-date=October 31, 2013}} He spent the rest of the 2011–12 season with the D-Fenders, playing in six regular season games and seven playoff games. After sitting out the entire 2012–13 season, Ingram returned to the D-Fenders for the 2013–14 season. In 45 games (11 starts) with the D-Fenders in 2013–14, Ingram posted averages of 9.1 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.7 assists, while shooting .447 from three-point range and helping the D-Fenders to a West Division Championship.{{cite web|url=http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/150112_ingramacquired/|title=D-Fenders Acquire Andrew [sic] Ingram|work=NBA.com|date=January 12, 2015|access-date=October 18, 2016|archive-date=December 21, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161221182302/http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/150112_ingramacquired/|url-status=dead}} Ingram did not return to the D-Fenders for the start of 2014–15 season. He missed the first two months of the season before joining the team on January 12, 2015. Ingram spent only his second full season with the D-Fenders in 2015–16. In February 2016, he became the D-League's all-time leader in three-pointers made and won his second three-point contest title. He took the crown by making 39-of-50 shots over two rounds – an all-time record across the NBA and D-League.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/andre-ingram-nba-dleague-three-point-contest-record/|title=Andre Ingram Makes Three-Point Contest Record 39 of 50 Shots to Take NBA D-League Crown|work=NBA.com|date=February 14, 2016|access-date=October 18, 2016}}{{cite web|last=Pincus|first=Eric|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-ln-d-fenders-andre-ingram-3-point-contest-20160219-story.html|title=D-Fenders' Andre Ingram impresses with win in D-League 3-point contest|work=Los Angeles Times|date=February 19, 2016|access-date=February 22, 2016}} ===Perth Wildcats (2016)=== On October 18, 2016, Ingram signed with the [[Perth Wildcats]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 NBL season]],{{cite web|url=http://www.wildcats.com.au/featured-news/perth-wildcats-sign-sharp-shooter-andre-ingram/|title=PERTH WILDCATS SIGN SHARP-SHOOTER ANDRE INGRAM|work=Wildcats.com.au|date=October 18, 2016|access-date=October 18, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170110213902/http://www.wildcats.com.au/featured-news/perth-wildcats-sign-sharp-shooter-andre-ingram/|archive-date=2017-01-10|url-status=dead}} marking his first stint overseas. However, he managed just two games for the Wildcats before requesting his release from the club a week after landing in Perth, citing mental health reasons for the sudden decision.{{cite web|url=http://www.wildcats.com.au/perth-wildcats/andre-ingram-departs-wildcats/|title=ANDRE INGRAM DEPARTS WILDCATS|work=Wildcats.com.au|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225101558/http://www.wildcats.com.au/perth-wildcats/andre-ingram-departs-wildcats/|archive-date=2017-02-25|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/33489/|title=WILDCATS SHOCKED BY INGRAM DEPARTURE|work=NBL.com.au|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016|archive-date=October 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161027054638/http://www.nbl.com.au/featured-news/33489/|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|last=Robinson|first=Chris|url=https://www.perthnow.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/perth-wildcats-import-andre-ingram-to-return-to-united-states-citing-mental-health-reasons-ng-fd0ee78ba3b017fd8bcab8803b0fd348|title=Perth Wildcats import Andre Ingram to return to United States, citing mental health reasons|work=PerthNow.com.au|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=April 15, 2018}} ===Return to D-Fenders / South Bay Lakers (2017–2018)=== On March 6, 2017, Ingram returned to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] to play out the 2016–17 season.{{cite web|url=http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/d-fenders-acquire-three-point-leader-andre-ingram/|title=D-Fenders Acquire Three-Point Leader Andre Ingram|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=March 6, 2017|archive-date=March 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307124137/http://losangeles.dleague.nba.com/news/d-fenders-acquire-three-point-leader-andre-ingram/|url-status=dead}} He returned to the team, now called the [[South Bay Lakers]], for the 2017–18 season. Ingram averaged 9.1 points, 2.5 rebounds and 1.1 assists in 47 games (seven starts) for the South Bay Lakers in 2017–18, shooting a league-best 47.5 percent from three-point range.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180409-andre-ingram-signed|title=Lakers Sign Andre Ingram for the Rest of the Season|work=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2018|access-date=April 9, 2018}} === Los Angeles Lakers (2018) === On April 9, 2018, Ingram signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the final two games of the [[2017–18 NBA season]]. He made his NBA debut the following day, scoring 19 points with four 3-pointers in a 105–99 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2018/04/11/sports/basketball/ap-bkn-rockets-lakers.html|title=CP3 Leads Rockets Past Lakers 105-99 for 31st Win in 34|work=nytimes.com|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=April 11, 2018}} At 32 years old, Ingram became the second oldest American rookie in the NBA since at least [[Pablo Prigioni]]’s 2012 rookie season at 35 years of age.{{clarify|date=January 2026}}{{cite web|last=Hoffman|first=Benjamin|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/04/10/sports/andre-ingram-lakers.html|title=Andre Ingram Got a Cup of Coffee and Turned it Into a Shooting Show|work=nytimes.com|date=April 10, 2018|access-date=April 11, 2018|quote=According to Basketball-Reference.com, the moment he stepped onto the court for Tuesday’s home loss to the Houston Rockets, Ingram became the oldest American rookie in the N.B.A. since at least 1964.}} His 19 points were the most by a Laker in his first career game since [[Nick Van Exel]] had 23 in 1993. For players making their NBA debut after the All-Star break, Ingram's 19 points were the most in a debut in 50 years, and the most scored by a Laker since [[Danny Finn]]'s 28 points in 1953.{{cite web|last=Youngmisuk|first=Ohm|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23110530/andre-ingram-los-angeles-lakers-scores-19-points-nba-debut-decade-g-league|title=G League call-up Andre Ingram scores 19 in NBA debut for Lakers|work=ESPN.com|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=April 11, 2018}} In the Lakers' season finale on April 11, Ingram scored five points on 2-of-9 shooting, including 1 of 4 from 3-point range, and had six assists and three rebounds in 35 minutes in a 115–100 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975974|title=Hart's 30 lead Lakers past Clippers 115-100 to end season|work=ESPN.com|date=April 11, 2018|access-date=April 11, 2018}} Ingram reportedly earned $13,824 for his three days with the Lakers, after making just $19,000 for the entirety of his G League season.{{cite web|last=Lauletta|first=Tyler|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/andre-ingram-lakers-g-league-salary-2018-4|title=The 32-year-old Lakers rookie who spent 10 years in the G League will nearly double his season salary in 3 days in the NBA|work=BusinessInsider.com|date=April 12, 2018|access-date=April 12, 2018}} ===Third stint with South Bay (2018–2019)=== Returning to the South Bay Lakers for the 2018–19 season,{{cite web |title=South Bay finalizes training camp roster and schedule |url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-finalizes-training-camp-roster-and-schedule/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 23, 2018 |date=October 20, 2018 |archive-date=October 23, 2018 web|last=Moreno|first=Matthew|url=https://www.lakersnation.com/south-bay-lakers-andre-ingram-g-league-all-time-leader-most-games-played/2019/01/13/|title=Andre Ingram Becomes G League All-Time Leader For Most Games Played|work=lakersnation.com|date=January 13, 2019|access-date=January 14, 2019}} ===Return to Los Angeles (2019)=== On March 11, 2019, Ingram signed a 10-day contract with the Los Angeles Lakers, returning to the franchise for a second stint.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/190310andre-ingram-10-day|title=Lakers Sign Andre Ingram|website=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=March 11, 2019}} With [[Lonzo Ball]] and [[Brandon Ingram]] out for the remainder of the season due to injuries, the Lakers roster required bolstering.{{cite web|last=Rapp|first=Timothy|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2825040-lakers-rumors-33-year-old-g-league-alum-andre-ingram-agrees-to-contract|title=33-Year-Old G League Alum Andre Ingram Agrees to Contract|work=bleacherreport.com|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=March 11, 2019}} ===Fourth stint with South Bay (2019–2022)=== After his 10-day contract expired, Ingram returned to South Bay for web|last=Young|first=Ryan|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/los-angeles-lakers-sending-andre-ingram-back-to-g-league-after-10-day-contract-231353441.html|title=Report: Lakers not renewing Andre Ingram's February 7, 2020, he was removed from the active roster due to a season-ending injury. He suffered a right [[Pectoralis major muscle|pectoralis tendon]] tear on January 22 and never fully recovered.{{cite news |title=Andre Ingram: Out with season-ending injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/andre-ingram-out-with-season-ending-injury/ |access-date=October 18, 2021 |work=cbssports.com |date=February 8, 2020}} In October 2020, Ingram was named as the inaugural president of the G League Players Union, known as the Basketball Players Union (BPU).{{cite web |url=https://www.talkbasket.net/108467-andre-ingram-named-president-of-g-league-players-association |title=Andre Ingram named president of G League Players Association |website=TalkBasketball |date=October 20, 2020}}{{cite web |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/258869/G-League-Players-Form-Union-With-Assistance-From-NBPA |title=G League Players Form Union With Assistance From NBPA |website=RealGM |date=July 21, 2020}} On October 23, 2021, Ingram was named to the training camp roster for the South Bay Lakers, returning to the franchise for a fifth stint.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Kioski|title=South Bay Finalizes Training Camp Roster|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-finalizes-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On December 19, 2021, Ingram was re-elected as President of the NBA G-League's union, following his stint as interim inaugural president.{{cite tweet|number=1472657975458336774|user=wojespn|title=ESPN Sources: Andre Ingram has been re-elected as President of the G-League's union. He will serve a two-year term.…|date=19 December 2021}} On April 10, 2022, he received his second [[Jason Collier Sportsmanship Award]].{{cite web|title=Andre Ingram Wins NBA G League Sportsmanship Award|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/andre-ingram-wins-nba-g-league-sportsmanship-award/|website=NBA.com|date=April 10, 2022|access-date=April 11, 2022}} ===Fifth stint with South Bay (2023)=== On March 8, 2023, Ingram was reacquired by the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/22-23-nba-g-league-transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022-23 NBA G League Transactions|date=March 8, 2023|access-date=March 8, 2023}} Ingram is considered to be retired but, he has expressed interest in returning to professional basketball.{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Sam |date=2024-07-12 |title=Beloved Former Laker Hoping for Comeback |url=https://www.si.com/nba/lakers/news/beloved-former-laker-hoping-for-comeback-01j2hy3d3a7g |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=Los Angeles Lakers On SI |language=en-US}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|leader=y}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2017}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
